result.title: VeriWorld: A Verifiable Visual SWE-Bench for Spatial Reasoning in 3D Environments
result.comment: 32 pages, 5 figures. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations and Datasets Track. Code at https://github.com/VITA-Group/VeriWorld and dataset at https://huggingface.co/datasets/yanyanzheng96/VeriWorld
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used for spatial tasks such as navigation and manipulation, where they must infer geometry and object relationships from visual input in order to act correctly. Existing benchmarks usually test perception and reasoning in isolation, making it hard to tell whether failures come from visual understanding, downstream reasoning, or the bridge between them. We introduce VeriWorld, a benchmark for spatial reasoning in interactive 3D environments with executable actions and deterministic verification. For task families where all three channels are well-defined, we evaluate matched visual, structured, and combined input conditions on the same instance, environment, and verifier; families without a clean visual/structured/combined split are reported separately. This design supports controlled comparisons of perception, reasoning, and their interaction. Using this setup, we uncover two diagnostic findings. First, models often perform much better when task-relevant information, such as object identity, current state, or target location, is given explicitly than when it must be read from the rendered scene, revealing a recurring visual-to-structure gap. Second, action-space and harness design can change outcomes even under the same task and information condition, showing that interaction protocol is itself a confounding variable. VeriWorld is open-sourced to support reproducible and fine-grained evaluation of spatial reasoning in VLMs.

AI.brief_summary: VeriWorld 是面向交互式 3D 环境空间推理的可验证基准，用可执行动作和确定性验证，在同一实例上对比纯视觉、结构化及组合输入，诊断 VLM 的感知、推理及其衔接失败。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「视觉到结构差距」与动作空间/harness 混杂直接关联 LVR 中视觉证据是否被内部使用、感知-推理接口及评价归因，可供核查视觉信息保留与贡献分配的实验设计。
